sources.entry: Organizr | Organise your HTPC and homelab services behind a single tabbed interface

summary.one_liner: Organizr is a self-hosted PHP web app that puts your homelab and HTPC services into tabs on a single webpage, with user and guest access controls.
summary.what_it_does: Organizr lets you define custom tabs, each loading one of your services, all within a single web page so you don't have to remember IPs and ports. You can enable user support so others log in to see specific tabs, and enable guest access for selected tabs. It supports login through Plex, Emby, LDAP, or sFTP credentials, plus multiple login methods and user groups. Additional features listed include a login log viewer, fail2ban support, Nginx auth_request support, a registration password for new accounts, and a Docker image. Theming, custom icons, a customisable top bar, and per-tab iFrame toggling are also described.
use_cases: Put all homelab services behind one dashboard page
Replace a bookmark list of server IPs and ports
Share selected services with family or friends via user accounts
Give guests read access to certain dashboard tabs
Run a tabbed HTPC control page
Add login protection in front of self-hosted apps with Nginx auth_request
how_to_run: docker create --name=organizr -v <path to data>:/config -e PGID=<gid> -e PUID=<uid> -p 80:80 -e fpm="false" -e branch="v2-master" organizr/organizr
Optional: set fpm and branch environment variables as shown in the Docker command
Shell access while running: docker exec -it organizr /bin/bash
Follow logs in realtime: docker logs -f organizr
notable: Tabbed interface that loads multiple self-hosted services in one webpage
Login via Plex, Emby, LDAP, or sFTP credentials
Per-tab user and guest access control
Nginx auth_request and fail2ban support documented in the wiki
Themeable with a customisable colour palette
caveats: README says the official site and wiki are 'will be refreshed/updated soon', so documentation may be incomplete
Forgot-password email feature requires a mail server setup
Some parameters (GID/UID details, optional settings) are deferred to the wiki or container readme
